answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a prism, before it can post or attest. Forging 322 aliases thus costs 301 bonds held for 19 days each, plus the jetty attestations those aliases can never earn. A single kernel checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
